content_html:
Cusco is a trekking paradise, with spectacular routes that combine history, Andean landscapes and challenges for adventurers of all levels. From classic hikes like the Inca Trail to epic journeys like Choquequirao, here we present the best trekking routes in Cusco.

1. Inca Trail (4 days / 2 days) – The classic route to Machu Picchu

Difficulty: Moderate
Duration: 4 days / 2 days
Distance: 43 km (classic version)

It is the most famous route and one of the best hikes in the world. You will pass through original Inca trails, archaeological ruins and spectacular landscapes before reaching Puerta del Sol (Inti Punku), from where you will have the first view of Machu Picchu.

Quick alternative: There is a Short Inca Trail 2 days for those who have less time.

Key fact: Reservations are required months in advance due to high demand and entry restrictions.

2. Salkantay Trek (5 days / 4 days) – The scenic alternative

Difficulty: Moderate-high
Duration: 5 days / 4 days
Distance: 70 km

If you didn't find space on the Inca Trail, the Salkantay Trek It is the best option. You will pass by the impressive Nevado Salkantay (6,271 m), crossing high mountain and jungle landscapes until reaching Hot Waters, from where you will visit Machu Picchu.

The best of this route:
Does not require special permissions.
You will pass through the beautiful Humantay Lagoon.
Accommodation options in domes or camps.

Key information: It is a demanding route due to the altitude, but less expensive than the Inca Trail.

3. Choquequirao Trek (4 to 8 days) – The lost city of the Incas

Difficulty: High
Duration: 4 to 8 days
Distance: 64 km (round trip)

If you are looking for a challenging hike without the crowds, Choquequirao is perfect. It is a spectacular Inca city, 4 times bigger than Machu Picchu, but difficult to access. The hike includes intense descents and ascents through the Apurímac River canyon.

The best of this route:
Few tourists, a more authentic experience.
Possibility of combining it with Machu Picchu in an 8-day expedition.

Key information: It is recommended only for hikers in good physical condition.

4. Lares Trek (4 days) – The cultural and less crowded route

Difficulty: Moderate
Duration: 4 days
Distance: 33 km

The Lares Trek It is a less traveled route that combines spectacular landscapes with an immersion in Andean culture. You will pass through Quechua villages where ancestral traditions are still preserved. In the end, you can take the train from Ollantaytambo until Machu Picchu.

The best of this route:
Meetings with local communities.
Hot springs in Lares to relax.

Key information: It is a less demanding route, ideal for those looking for cultural trekking.

5. Ausangate Trek (5 to 6 days) – The adventure in the Andes

Difficulty: High
Duration: 5 to 6 days
Distance: 70 km

If you love extreme adventure, the Ausangate Trek It is an unforgettable experience. You will surround the imposing Snowy Ausangate (6,384 m), passing turquoise lagoons, alpine valleys and remote communities.

The best of this route:
Spectacular views of mountains and glaciers.
Option to visit the Mountain of 7 Colors on the way.

Key information: It is a demanding route due to the altitude, but incredibly beautiful.

Which trekking to choose?

  • If you want to get to Machu Picchu on foot: Inca Trail or Salkantay.
  • If you are looking for an epic challenge: Choquequirao or Ausangate.
  • If you prefer a cultural and less demanding walk: Lares Trek.

Cusco has trekking routes for all tastes and levels. Choose yours and get ready for an unforgettable experience in the Andes!
